title: Design System: Agentic Skills / Security Proof

display.purpose: Artifact title only; condensed, uppercase, and tightly set.

headline.purpose: The single claim that opens each evidence stage.

title.purpose: Names contained proofs, techniques, platforms, and result groups.

body.purpose: Readable explanations and explicit claim boundaries.

label.purpose: Metadata, codes, stages, scores, commands, and control labels.

shadows.name: offset-sheet
shadows.purpose: The only ambient shadow; separates the complete proof artifact from the canvas.

motion.name: stage-settle
motion.purpose: Introduces the newly selected evidence panel with a short upward settle.

motion.name: runtime-event
motion.purpose: Reveals correlated runtime nodes, with a 350ms stagger on the later node.

components.name: Stage Button
components.description: A numbered route control for moving through the eight evidence stages.
components.css: .ds-stage-button { display:grid; grid-template-columns:34px 1fr; gap:12px; align-items:center; min-height:56px; padding:7px 8px 7px 0; color:#101c2d; border:0; background:transparent; font:800 .92rem/1.05 "Arial Narrow",Arial,sans-serif; text-align:left; text-transform:uppercase; cursor:pointer; } .ds-stage-dot { display:grid; place-items:center; width:34px; height:34px; border:2px solid #101c2d; background:#e9e4d8; font:800 .7rem/1 ui-monospace,monospace; } .ds-stage-button:hover .ds-stage-dot { background:#fffdf7; } .ds-stage-button:focus-visible { outline:3px solid #00637c; outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Current Stage Button
components.description: The active trace marker uses warning orange and a matching text cue.
components.css: .ds-stage-button { display:grid; grid-template-columns:34px 1fr; gap:12px; align-items:center; min-height:56px; padding:7px 8px 7px 0; color:#101c2d; border:0; background:transparent; font:800 .92rem/1.05 "Arial Narrow",Arial,sans-serif; text-align:left; text-transform:uppercase; cursor:pointer; } .ds-stage-dot { display:grid; place-items:center; width:34px; height:34px; border:2px solid #101c2d; background:#e9e4d8; font:800 .7rem/1 ui-monospace,monospace; } .ds-current { color:#ad3515; } .ds-current .ds-stage-dot { color:#fffdf7; border-color:#ad3515; background:#ad3515; } .ds-stage-button:focus-visible { outline:3px solid #00637c; outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Proof Action
components.description: A high-contrast action placed on a register-ink evidence bar.
components.html: SIX EVENTS / THREE SESSIONS
components.css: .ds-action-bar { display:flex; justify-content:space-between; gap:16px; align-items:center; padding:14px 16px; color:#fffdf7; background:#101c2d; font:900 1.35rem/1 "Arial Narrow",Arial,sans-serif; } .ds-proof-action { min-height:42px; padding:.6rem 1rem; color:#fffdf7; border:2px solid #fffdf7; background:transparent; font:900 .7rem/1.2 ui-monospace,monospace; text-transform:uppercase; cursor:pointer; } .ds-proof-action:hover { color:#101c2d; background:#fffdf7; } .ds-proof-action:focus-visible { outline:3px solid #00637c; outline-offset:3px; }

components.name: Navigation Button
components.description: A compact previous or next control anchored to the lower proof rule.
components.css: .ds-nav-button { min-width:92px; min-height:38px; padding:.45rem .7rem; color:#101c2d; border:1px solid #101c2d; background:transparent; font:900 .68rem/1.3 ui-monospace,monospace; text-transform:uppercase; cursor:pointer; } .ds-nav-button:hover { color:#fffdf7; background:#101c2d; } .ds-nav-button:focus-visible { outline:3px solid #00637c; outline-offset:3px; } .ds-nav-button:disabled { opacity:.35; cursor:not-allowed; }

components.name: Evidence Card
components.description: A square, ruled proof block that keeps a technical claim adjacent to its explanation.
components.html:
DEFENSE EVASION / REPRESENTATION

ENCODED INSTRUCTIONS

Decode bounded printable content, then reapply the same rules.
components.css: .ds-evidence-card { padding:24px; color:#101c2d; border:1px solid #101c2d; background:#fffdf7; font:400 16px/1.5 -apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,"Segoe UI",Arial,sans-serif; } .ds-evidence-card small { color:#00637c; font:800 .67rem/1.4 ui-monospace,monospace; letter-spacing:.08em; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-evidence-card h3 { margin:.3rem 0 .8rem; font:900 2rem/.95 "Arial Narrow",Arial,sans-serif; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-evidence-card p { margin:0; }

components.name: Verification Stamp
components.description: A slightly rotated double-line stamp for verified stage outcomes.
components.css: .ds-proof-stamp { display:inline-block; padding:.45rem .65rem; color:#087a50; border:3px double currentColor; background:transparent; font:900 .72rem/1.2 ui-monospace,monospace; letter-spacing:.08em; text-transform:uppercase; transform:rotate(-2deg); }

components.name: Warning Stamp
components.description: The orange stamp variant marks a false negative, caution, synthetic fixture, or claim boundary.
components.css: .ds-proof-stamp { display:inline-block; padding:.45rem .65rem; color:#087a50; border:3px double currentColor; background:transparent; font:900 .72rem/1.2 ui-monospace,monospace; letter-spacing:.08em; text-transform:uppercase; transform:rotate(-2deg); } .ds-proof-stamp.ds-warn { color:#ad3515; }

components.name: Pass Status
components.description: A square, unrotated status label used inside structured platform ledgers.
components.css: .ds-status-pass { display:inline-block; padding:.35rem .5rem; color:#087a50; border:2px solid currentColor; background:transparent; font:900 .7rem/1.2 ui-monospace,monospace; text-align:center; text-transform:uppercase; }

narrative.overview:
The interface behaves like a print-production proof sheet prepared for technical review: warm paper, crop marks, registration color, measured rules, editorial annotations, and stamped outcomes. It feels investigative and handmade enough to be memorable, but never theatrical; the visual authority comes from visible evidence, explicit boundaries, and a disciplined sequence rather than from a generic dark security-dashboard aesthetic.

The system is built for explanation. Condensed headlines announce the current claim, monospace labels expose its provenance and state, and a neutral reading face carries the reasoning. Cyan registers structure, green verifies observed outcomes, and orange marks failures, warnings, active steps, and unresolved boundaries. Every visual state must remain legible without color and every factual claim stays adjacent to the evidence that supports it.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, physical proof-sheet surfaces framed by crop marks, rules, ticks, ledgers, and stamps.
A three-voice type system: condensed display, neutral body, and monospace evidence labels.
Flat, square geometry with one deliberately offset sheet shadow and no decorative rounding.
Sparse semantic color: cyan for registration, green for verification, and orange for attention or failure.
Sequential evidence presentation that keeps navigation, stage, and claim status visible together.

rules.name: The Evidence Color Rule
rules.body: Cyan means registration, green means verified, and orange means attention; never interchange these roles for decoration.

rules.name: The Ink Before Accent Rule
rules.body: Structural lines and headings use register ink first. Accent color appears only where it adds state, provenance, or navigation meaning.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Condensed type states the claim, body type explains it, and monospace type proves or operates it.

rules.name: The One Claim Rule
rules.body: Each evidence panel opens with one large headline; supporting labels stay small enough that they cannot compete with it.

rules.name: The Claim Beside Proof Rule
rules.body: A conclusion and its supporting artifact share the same panel; do not force the reader to remember evidence from another screen.

rules.name: The Trace Survives Rule
rules.body: Responsive changes may rotate or stack the route, but they must preserve all seven stages and their reading order.

rules.name: The One Sheet Shadow Rule
rules.body: Never add drop shadows to evidence cards, controls, stamps, or rows; use rules, tone, or reversed ink instead.

rules.name: The No Soft Corners Rule
rules.body: Rounded cards and pill badges break the proof-sheet metaphor; keep components square, including compact status labels.

dos: Do attach every claim to a visible score, code sample, ledger row, boundary statement, or reproduction command.
Do use the condensed/body/monospace hierarchy consistently so claims, reasoning, and evidence remain distinguishable.
Do reserve cyan, green, and orange for their named semantic roles and reinforce every color state with text or shape.
Do preserve the seven-stage trace, visible focus, keyboard operation, reduced motion, and the complete print view.
Do use rules, paper tones, and reversed ink to create hierarchy inside the sheet.
donts: Don't convert the interface into a dark, glowing, metric-card security dashboard.
Don't use rounded cards, pill badges, gradients, glass effects, or decorative shadows.
Don't present a Benign label, score, or platform result without its explicit claim boundary.
Don't detach failure from improvement; the V1 miss and V2 decoded-layer change belong in the same comparison.
Don't animate for spectacle or leave hidden stages unavailable in the print artifact.
